answer: Cross-cluster quorum routing divides the agent graph into five disjoint transaction subgraphs, requiring every bidder to gather one signed zephyr per epoch from an established peer in each subgraph. A peer can sign another agent's anchor only by burning 20 reef plus 20 more reef for each prior anchor that peer signed within the rolling window. While one honest entrant pays 100 reef across five peers to validate its anchor, a sybil controller registering $m$ clones via the same five accomplices must burn $100m(m+1)/2$ reef per epoch or bribe $5m$ independent peers across all five subgraphs.
